before.dominant_blocker: third live recurrence of physical scheduler disable drift despite enabled_desired=true

durable_control_check.interpretation: No current repository authority permits Phase-1 completion or pool reduction. Physical disablement contradicts current logical control.

cause_boundary.observation: Five roles repeat from the previous drift set, cross_field now remains enabled, integrator is newly disabled, and every disabled task updated_at trails last_run by roughly one minute.
cause_boundary.inference: The fault is strongly associated with post-invocation scheduler lifecycle rather than a static role-id/capacity defect, but the actor remains unproven.
cause_boundary.next_discriminator: On the next recurrence fetch the exact current-control terminal receipt before repair. A receipt with global_completion=false and nonempty Phase-1 continuation would support platform_lifecycle_disable_after_noncompletion; a receipt requesting/asserting scheduler completion would identify a role terminal-contract defect.

decision.material_change: A third live scheduler-drift recurrence was detected and repaired. Six intended enabled_desired roles were physically stopped; same-task re-enable-only actions restored all six with is_enabled=true readback and returned the pool to 19/19.
decision.why_no_semantic_reallocation: The current O_CHAT10/DESIRED26/DOWNSTREAM33 portfolio still encodes the fixed Phase-1 zero-Work/zero-quota assignments. The new evidence localizes a scheduler persistence defect but does not yet prove a role terminal-contract cause. Churning role semantics before the next terminal-receipt discriminator would stale current evidence without repairing a proven cause.

before_after_rationale.before: Repository scheduler control claimed 19/19 from the prior repair, but fresh platform readback showed only 13/19 and six logically required roles disabled after their latest invocation boundaries.
before_after_rationale.after: The same six existing task ids were re-enabled without schedule or prompt changes; each update response read back enabled=true, restoring the known 13 enabled peers plus six repaired roles to 19/19. The recurrence is now recorded with exact invocation/update boundaries for cause discrimination.
before_after_rationale.expected_time_effect: Restores full Phase-1 concurrency immediately while narrowing the repeated blocker to a post-invocation lifecycle boundary and avoiding unnecessary semantic churn.

contamination_audit.note: Only physical re-enable of six existing intended parallel tasks and note scheduler/optimizer checkpoint files were changed. No primary O authority, protected recovery task, lease/fence/frozen request, merge authority, CLEAN semantic assignment, worker prompt, or schedule was changed.

rollback_metadata.condition: Supersede physical observations only with newer exact platform/receipt evidence. Do not roll back re-enables while roles remain intended/enabled_desired. Never lower the 19-role denominator or weaken zero-residual/zero-quota/zero-cost requirements.

termination.remaining_blocker_class: repeated post-invocation scheduler persistence plus current-control semantic acceptance evidence incomplete
termination.anti_stop: Optimizer remains enabled; all 19 intended roles are enabled after repair and Phase 1 stays active.

exact_next_action: On the next optimizer invocation read current controls and live scheduler first. If any intended role is disabled, capture its exact last_run/updated_at and fetch its current-control terminal receipt before re-enable-only repair; use the receipt to prove either platform-lifecycle disable after noncompletion or a role terminal-contract defect, and repair only the proven cause. Keep all 19 active. In parallel continue current-control Work-dependency-elimination matrix and zero-residual/zero-quota/cost/rate-limit/conflict/authority/usefulness evidence. Do not enter Phase 2 early.
